This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
On 27.02.2024 at about 08-00 pm., the petitioner was proceeding in a Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02- HB-9883 towards Garuda Park from Eshwara Temple, and when he reached near Laggere Junction road, J.C Nagar-Kurubarahalli, Pipelane road, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-8261 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Chord road Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient from 27-02-2024 to 02-03-2024.

So far,
the petitioner has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medicine, traveling expenses and he has to spent huge amount towards future treatment.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was working as Sales Manager at K2 Hoists and Cranes and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work.

He has suffered pain and sufferings,
permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

Madhava Shriyan vs Rudra Gouda on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186481928/
2
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent no.2/the Insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-8261 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the petition is bad for non joinder of proper and necessary parties and that the driver of the Insured car was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having Fitness certificate.

It is further contended that the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg No.KA-02-HB- 9883 as the rider of the said motor cycle came from opposite direction in a zigzag manner and without wearing helmet and without observing any rules dashed to the right side of the Insured vehicle which was moving on the extreme left side of the main road and therefore the rider of the motor cycle was 100% negligent in riding his vehicle.
The respondent no.2 further contended that there is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint.
The jurisdictional police by colluding with the claimant has filed a false case against the respondent.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 27-02-2024 at about 8-00 p.m, when he was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-HB-9883 towards Garuda Park from Eshwara Temple on JC Nagar - Kurubarahalli, Pipelane Road, Laggere Junction Road at that time, the driver of Car bearing registration No.KA- 05-MX-8261 drove the same from Lotus Hospital side at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Motor Cycle.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P23.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order,

3  for the following;
 REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-MX-8261, the P.W.1 has filed him affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 27.02.2024 at about 08-00 pm., when the petitioner was proceeding in a Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HB- 9883 towards Garuda Park from Eshwara Temple, and when he reached near Laggere Junction road, J.C Nagar-Kurubarahalli, Pipelane road, at that time

the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MX-8261 (herein after called the offending vehicle)
came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 12 which are the police records such as FIR, complaint, statement of eye witness, statement of victim, spot sketch, Spot mahazar, notice u/Sec 133 of MV Act, reply notice, Notice of arrest of accused, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Kavya., case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0061/2024 by Rajajinagar Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
After completion of investigation, the Investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IMV act.
13. So far as the objection raised by the respondent no.2 regarding the delay in lodging the complaint is concerned, the accident in question has occurred on 27-02-2024 at 8-00 pm.,
The complaint came to be lodged on 28-02-2024 at 3-00 pm.,
There is less than one day delay in lodging the complaint and the said delay would no way effect the case of the petitioner.

Further if the police intimation and MLC produced by the petitioner is perused, soon after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to the hospital wherein the history of injury is mentioned as "RTA near Laggere circle on 27-02-2024".
Hence, it can be said that the petitioner has sustained injury due to the accident and because of his taking treatment as an inpatient there was delay in lodging the compliant.
Further when police intimation was send from the hospital authority it is for the jurisdiction police to attend the petitioner by visiting the hospital and to record the statement of the petitioner.

14. So far as the allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the spot mahazar and sketch at Ex.P4 and 5 are perused, the petitioner who was proceeding from Eshwara Temple was taking right turn to proceed towards Garuda statue.
The offending vehicle which came from Lotus Hospital side in order to go towards Laggere side took the vehicle towards right side and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Hence, the spot of accident shown in the sketch clearly reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle by driving his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner.

Though the respondent no.2 has seriously contended that the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle is the cause for accident but respondent no.2 has not Madhava Shriyan vs Rudra Gouda on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186481928/
4 taken steps to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent act contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P.11 and Ex.P14.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 27.02.2024 to 02.03.2024 at Chord Road Hospital Pvt Ltd, Bangalore for a period of 5 days.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries of which injury no.1 is grievous in nature and injury no.2 and 3 are simple in nature.

16. Balavva.G Balabatti - Chord Road Hospital Pvt Ltd., Bangalore, is examined as PW2 and through him Police intimation, MLC, case sheet and X-ray films are marked as Ex.P.18 to 21.
17.
Dr. Ullas Mahesh., - visiting Consultant, Depart of Orthopedics at Nandi Clini, Bangalore is examined as Pw.3 and through him X-ray report and Medical prescription are marked as Ex.P22 and 23.
The P.W.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 28.10.2025 for assessment of disability.
PW.3 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 48% and to the whole body at 16%.
18. If the cross examination of PW.3 is carefully perused, PW.3 is not a treated doctor.
As per the evidence of the PW.3 the fracture injury is united but implant is in situ and there is no shortening of right lower limb and petitioner can do his work in a sitting posture.

Hence, considering the evidence of PW.3 this court inclines to assess the disability of petitioner on whole body at 12% instead of 16%.
19.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
20. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
21. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bills for Rs.1,82,304/- as per Ex.P15.
The respondent has not much disputed the genuineness of the medical bills and there is no even any reason to dispute the correctness of the medical bills.

Hence,
petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,82,304/-.
22.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 41 years.
He was working as Sales Manager and drawing salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m..
But to substantiate the said contention, petitioner has not produced any materials.
Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner, taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Madhava Shriyan vs Rudra Gouda on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186481928/
5 23.
The petitioner has sustained five grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 5 days as inpatient at Chord Road Hospital Pvt Ltd, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 3 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for three month.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.49,500/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .
24. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Chord Road Hospital Pvt Ltd, Bangalore.
Further for taking treatment as inpatient in the said hospital he was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
25 . The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 41 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced his Aadhar card which is marked as Ex.P13, which shows his date of birth as 01.06.1982 that means he was aged about 42 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar Card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 42 years.

26. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.3 even though he has assessed disability on higher side, but this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 12% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 42 years, as per Sarla Varma's case, the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.
So by applying the multiplier '14' the future loss of income due to disability would comes to Rs.3,32,640/- (i.e., 16,500 x 12% x 14 x 12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,32,640/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
27. The petitioner at his age of 42 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 1,82,304/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 49,500/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5. Loss of Future Income Rs. 3,32,640/-
6. loss of comfort and amenities Rs. 30,000/-

Total Rs. 6,84,444/-
Madhava Shriyan vs Rudra Gouda on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186481928/
6
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,84,444/- (Rupees Six Lakh Eighty Four Thousand Four Hundred Forty Four only).
28. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent No.2 this Tribunal directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
29. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER  The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,84,444/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Eighty Four Thousand Four Hundred Forty Four only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
